name: Wyatt
tagline: Got his wires crossed. Both currents.

romance_success.title: You Light Up My Life
romance_success.text: Wyatt is grounded, up to code and absolutely gone on you. The lights never flicker anymore, except when you walk into the room. That part, he insists, is not a wiring problem.

romance_failure.title: Short Circuit
romance_failure.text: Wyatt left with his extension cord and his dignity. He's doing great, actually. He's a licensed electrician now. He is very, very good. He does not take your calls.

friend_success.title: Current Besties
friend_success.text: Wyatt is your best friend and the most enthusiastic house-sitter alive. He finally told Tyler how he feels. Tyler said his outfit was 'a choice.' It's going well.

friend_failure.title: Disconnected
friend_failure.text: Wyatt cut the power on his way out. Nobody knows how. Your fridge has been making a sad little noise ever since.

lines: *The fuse box pops. Sparks rain down. A lanky guy with static-fluffed hair stumbles out, patting out a small fire on his sleeve.*
Whoa! Hi! Hello! Sorry. Is this the bathroom? I'm looking for the bathroom.
You: This is the living room.
Right. Right right right. Crossed wires. Happens constantly. I'm Wyatt. Like 'wire it.' Like, wire it [wrong].

choices.text: Hi, Wyatt. You're kind of... electric.
Are you the reason my lights flicker?
You just set my wall on fire.

lines: I've been installed upside down since 1974. Everything I say comes out a little backwards. Wait. Reverse that.
*A lamp across the room turns on, then off, then on, apologetically.*
Anyway! What were we talking about? I forgot. Short-term memory. Short circuit. Short— I'm short-circuiting.

choices.text: You're kind of... electric.
Are you the reason my lights flicker?
You just set my wall on fire.

lines: *His hair stands straight up. Literally. Static.*
Electric? Me? Oh, you're— okay, you're making my current do a thing.
Is it hot in here? It might be me. I'm technically a fire hazard.
Oh! Yes. Sorry. That's me thinking. When I think really hard, the bulbs go *bzzt*.
When I get a crush, the whole block browns out. Last time, three streetlights exploded. Her name was Dana.
Also his name was Marco. Different crushes. Same streetlights.
It's a small fire! It's a starter fire. Fires gotta start somewhere!
*He stomps on it. It goes out. Mostly.*
Okay, that one's on me. Everything's always a little bit on me.
This was nice. I think? My readings are all over the place.
Come back? Please come back. It gets lonely in the box.
*Wyatt is sitting cross-legged on the floor, tangled in what appears to be his own extension cord.*
{player}! You came back! I rehearsed what to say. I forgot all of it. Hi.

choices.text: Tell me about these crushes of yours.
Here, let me help you untangle.
You're a mess, Wyatt.

lines: Oh, I'm very [AC/DC|acdc]. Both currents. Equal-opportunity sparks.
Guys, girls, enbies, one really attractive toaster. Look. It was a good toaster.

choices.text: Same, honestly.
And what about me?
What about the pink tile guy in the bathroom?

lines: Alternating current, direct current. I contain multitudes. And also about forty amps.
So yeah. That's me. What about you?

choices.text: Same, honestly.
And what about me?

lines: *His whole face lights up. Like, actually. There's a glow.*
Bi-five!
*He holds up his hand. You high-five him. You both get a mild shock.*
Worth it.
You? Oh. Oh no. Okay. Um.
*Every lamp in the house flickers at once.*
...Did that answer your question?
Tyler? Pink Tyler? Tyler with the opinions about grout?
*He goes very pink himself.*
He told me my wiring was 'tragically pre-war.' Nobody's ever insulted my wiring that confidently. I think about it constantly.
*You start unwinding the cord. Your hands brush. Somewhere, something goes bzzt.*
Sorry! Sorry. That was me. That's a thing my body does. When someone's nice to me.
You're very... [grounding]. Did you know that?
Like a third prong. Like a copper rod in wet soil. Like— that's the most romantic thing I know how to say, okay?
I KNOW. I'm a mess! I'm a HOT mess! Literally! I run at like ninety degrees!
*He deflates a little.*
...Most people just flip my breaker and walk away. At least you said it to my face.
Okay, I have to go recharge. That's not a metaphor. I need to sit in the box for a while.
Come back soon? I'll try to remember your name. {player}. {player}. Got it. Probably.
*Wyatt is pacing. Little sparks follow his footsteps like nervous puppies.*
Okay, so I looked it up. If you fix me, I get rewired. Up to code. Grounded. [Boring|boring].
Will you still like me if I don't randomly shock you?

choices.text: I like you for you. Not for the sparks.
You'll always be my favorite weirdo.
Honestly? I'd prefer not getting electrocuted.
You should tell Tyler how you feel.

lines: Boring! Like a nice beige outlet. Like a guy who reads instruction manuals for fun.
...Actually that sounds kind of nice? Is that bad? I'm confused. I'm always confused.
So? Be honest. My voltage can take it. Probably.

choices.text: I like you for you. Not for the sparks.
You'll always be my favorite weirdo.
Honestly? I'd prefer not getting electrocuted.

lines: *He stops pacing. The sparks stop too.*
Not for the sparks. Huh.
Nobody's ever liked me *despite* the sparks before. They either liked the danger, or they called an electrician.
*He leans in and kisses you. It's soft and a little tingly, like licking a nine-volt battery, but in a good way.*
Favorite weirdo! I'm somebody's favorite weirdo!
*He hugs you. Your hair stands on end. You both look like dandelions now.*
Right. No. Totally fair. Safety first.
*The sparks fizzle out.*
I'll just... dim myself. I'm good at that.
Tell Tyler? TYLER? He'd destroy me. He'd critique my font. I don't even HAVE a font.
...But you think I should?
*He looks toward the bathroom like it's the moon.*
Okay. After I'm fixed. When I'm grounded. I'll be brave. Maybe.
Next time, I think I'm ready. Flip my switch.
Wait, that sounded weird. Rewire me. Professionally.
*Wyatt stands by the open fuse box, holding out a pair of wire strippers with both hands.*
Okay. Okay okay okay. I'm ready. Probably.
Red to red, black to black, and try not to look me in the eyes or I'll short out.

choices.text: You turn me on, Wyatt. Literally and otherwise.
I like you. But this whole thing is a fire hazard.
Let's do this, buddy. Together.
Hold still and stop sparking.

lines: *You work carefully. He holds very, very still, which is the hardest thing he has ever done.*
*Click. Hum. Every light in the house comes on at once, warm and steady.*
I'm... grounded. I'm GROUNDED. I can THINK! I know where the bathroom is!
And I know exactly where I want to be. Which is here. With you. Steadily. At a reasonable voltage.

v4_rs2.fxText: The lights went out. On purpose, this time.
lines: ...Best power outage of my life.
*You rewire him in silence. Click. Hum. The lights steady.*
...Fire hazard. Yeah. I heard that.
Funny. Now that I'm grounded I can actually see things clearly. And clearly, you liked the idea of me more than me.
*He unplugs himself from the wall, coils up his cord with great dignity and walks out the front door.*
*Click. Hum. The lights steady. Wyatt blinks like he's waking up.*
Whoa. Whoa! I remember things! I remember your birthday!
I don't know when your birthday is. But I'll remember it once you tell me!
Buddies. Best buddies. Grounded, up-to-code best buddies.
*Click. Hum. The lights steady. Wyatt flexes his fingers. No sparks.*
Huh. Quiet in here now.
Oh! Hi! Again! I'm still processing the last conversation. My circuits are full.
Come back next week? I'll try to remember what we talked about. No promises.
Hey you. The lights are steady, my head is clear, and I still can't stop thinking about you. Diagnosis: not a wiring problem.
*Wyatt is packing spare fuses into a box. He doesn't look up.*
Just grabbing my stuff. Your wiring's fine. It's up to code. Like I said: you liked the idea of me.
Buddy! I told Tyler. He said my jacket was 'a choice.' I think that means yes?!
*Wyatt stares at you, perfectly grounded and perfectly cold.*
Power's on. That's all you wanted, right?
